structure:
A single Markdown ruling file (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-23.md) from Ian, dated 23 November 2026, answering whether the live animals and high-risk plants party pickers list every address for a role on one page. It opens with the bug report that raised it, quotes inc-087's acceptance criterion 7 under "What was asked", and then rules in seven numbered points under "Decided": the paging figure and the clause dropped, the distillation error identified, the same ruling settling the opposite answer three lines above, the prototype's single page as a fixture, the restatement of the chosen address returning, req-611 left alone, and inc-087 staying done. Scope is the whole file; nothing is left out. It is one part.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Whole ruling: Read the whole ruling file ruling-ian-2026-11-23.md in full: the bug report quoted at the top, inc-087's criterion 7 quoted under "What was asked", and the seven numbered points under "Decided". Each numbered point was read for the decisions it carries, and a point holding more than one decision is split into one claim per decision, so point 1's paging figure, dropped clause, precedent refusal and relation to role filtering are separate claims. The ruling leaves nothing open on what it touches except what the pickers do once a search narrows a long list, which is recorded as a gap claim.

claims.statement: The live animals and high-risk plants party pickers show eight of a role's addresses a page.
claims.quote: The pickers page at eight, and the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.note: New. Answers the report question the bug raised against inc-087 criterion 7.

claims.statement: The one-page clause of inc-087's acceptance criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.quote: the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped
claims.note: New. The clause this ruling withdraws, named by criterion.

claims.statement: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses, which is why the pickers take it.
claims.quote: Eight is the figure the INS address book list already uses (`insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49`, `REQ-INS-ADDR-013`).

claims.statement: The animals transporter list is not a precedent for how many addresses a page holds, because it renders no pagination today and the ticket to split it into pages of eight is still to do.
claims.quote: The animals transporter list is **not** a precedent: it renders no pagination today, and EUDPA-824, the ticket to split it into pages of eight, is still To Do.
claims.note: New. Refuses a precedent rather than setting one.

claims.statement: Paging the pickers sits on top of the role filtering, which stays as it is.
claims.quote: Paging comes back on top of the role filtering, which is correct and stays.
claims.note: New. Leaves the role filtering inc-087 built untouched.

claims.statement: The one-page clause was a distillation error: it rests on a claim that is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle on live filtering, not a ruling of Sam's on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: **It was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.** The clause rests on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041`, which is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle, not a ruling of Sam's on paging
claims.note: New. Names the claim the withdrawn clause rested on.

claims.statement: Sam's point 3b rules on when results refresh, not on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: It rules on when results refresh, not on how many a page holds.
claims.note: New. The ground on which the earlier claim is read as not covering paging.

claims.statement: The same afternoon ruling builds the INS address book list at eight a page three lines above the sentence that removed the pickers' paging, over the same address-book records, so one page of it holds two incompatible answers, and eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.quote: One ruling, one page of it, two incompatible answers to how many addresses a page holds. Eight is the one with a requirement behind it.

claims.statement: The prototype showing one page of addresses is a fixture of an address book too small to need paging, not a requirement that a page holds every address.
claims.quote: **The prototype's single page is a fixture, not a requirement.** `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063` reads one page off the prototype's own address book, which holds too few records to need paging, so the prototype could not show paging whether it wanted it or not.
claims.note: New. Sets aside the prototype claim behind the one-page clause.

claims.statement: How many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel, so the prototype is not the authority for it.
claims.quote: It rests instead on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116`, "Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected": how many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel
claims.note: New. Says which earlier claim point 4 rests on, and which it does not.

claims.statement: The "Selected address: <name>" restatement comes back with the paging, between the search box and the results, in the words both frontends already had.
claims.quote: The inset goes back where it was, between the search box and the results, with the words both frontends already had.
claims.note: New. Reverses req-595's removal of the inset.

claims.statement: The reason req-595 gave for dropping the restatement no longer holds, because the chosen row can be on another page again and a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.quote: Once the chosen row can be on another page again, that reason is gone: a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.note: New. Why the inset returns rather than merely that it does.

claims.statement: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display.
claims.quote: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display. Paging the API would make the role filter wrong.
claims.note: New. Leaves req-611 as it is.

claims.statement: inc-087 stays done, because it was built as its criteria then read, and the code, the criteria, the requirements behind them, c-094's outcome and the behaviour spec are corrected under EUDPA-827 so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.
claims.quote: **`inc-087` stays done.** It was built as its criteria then read. The code is corrected under EUDPA-827, which also corrects the criteria, the requirements behind them, `c-094`'s outcome and the behaviour spec, so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.
claims.note: New. Says the increment is not reopened and where the correction lands.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what the pickers offer once a search narrows a role's list to eight or fewer, so whether pagination disappears on a narrowed list is left open here.
claims.note: New. The ruling fixes the page size and the restatement but says nothing about a search narrowing the list below the threshold; the behaviour spec settles it.
